title: How to Read Nutrition Labels for Better Weight Health Understanding

authorship.current_visible_author: Healthy Weight Literacy Foundation Editorial Team
authorship.recommended_normalized_author: Healthy Weight Literacy Foundation Editorial Team

primary_question: How do I read a nutrition label to make informed food choices for weight health?
reader_intent: Understand every major section of a Nutrition Facts label (serving size, calories, fats, sodium, carbs, protein, vitamins, %DV) and use it to compare products.
desired_reader_outcome: Reader can read a full nutrition label end-to-end and use %DV to compare products.

claims.proposition: Recommended limits: cholesterol <300mg/day (<200mg with heart disease); sodium <2,300mg/day; fiber 25-30g/day; added sugars <50g/day (ideally <25g).
claims.recommended_action: Standard, widely published guideline figures (consistent with Dietary Guidelines/AHA benchmarks) but stated with zero citation.

disposition_reason: The most comprehensive of the two near-duplicate label-reading articles (covers vitamins/minerals and protein-per-meal guidance the other omits) and selected as cluster survivor, but has zero citations for several specific numeric guideline thresholds.
required_research: Cite Dietary Guidelines for Americans / AHA / FDA label-format sources directly for each numeric threshold.
recommended_rewrite_scope: Fold in reading-nutrition-labels-what-to-look-for's FDA-2020-format-update framing and front-of-package marketing-claims section, which this article omits.
